teacherPlayback: Two complete playbacks controlled by the teacher. No student media controls.
scoreRule: 6 objectively scored multiple-choice tasks and 2 teacher-reviewed written tasks, 1 point each. Proposed grade only after both written tasks reviewed.
notes: Authentic dialogue includes aggression and profanity. Teacher must check age suitability and source recording.

objective.q: Why does the man give so many rules?
options: He wants to organise a football game
He is explaining a school task
He wants to plan a business meeting
He wants the wedding to pass without trouble
objective.explanation: The rules are intended to prevent problems during the celebration.
objective.sourceEvidence: He wants the wedding day to be peaceful.

objective.q: What makes his speech difficult to finish?
options: Other men keep interrupting him
The ceremony begins too early
He has forgotten the rules
The music becomes too loud
objective.explanation: The other men interrupt with objections and questions.

objective.q: Why does one man object to the guests' clothes?
options: He thinks they are too expensive
He wants to wear a different suit
He dislikes the uniforms he sees
He thinks they should wear hats
objective.explanation: One man protests that there are uniforms.
objective.sourceEvidence: A complaint concerns uniforms despite an earlier promise.

objective.q: What does the speaker do after the surprise question?
options: He ends the meeting
He says no and continues his warnings
He asks the bride for advice
He changes the wedding date
objective.explanation: He refuses repeatedly and goes on with restrictions.
objective.sourceEvidence: A question about snow triggers further rules.

objective.q: What does the speaker especially want to avoid?
options: Having to give another speech
The guests arriving too early
Having too much food
Embarrassing Grace
objective.explanation: He invokes Grace as a reason to behave.
objective.sourceEvidence: He says not to embarrass Grace.

objective.q: Why does his final instruction sound so strong?
options: He repeats it more and more loudly
He changes it into a song
He makes everyone repeat it
He stops before finishing
objective.explanation: Repetition and volume make the order forceful.
objective.sourceEvidence: The final order is repeated loudly.

written.q: Write one person's first name from the conversation.
written.teacherCriterion: Accept one name clearly heard in the clip.
written.sourceEvidence: Grace, John and Charlie are named.

written.q: Give one reason why the event might become difficult.
written.modelAnswer: The different groups dislike one another, or the uniforms could cause trouble.
written.teacherCriterion: One specific source of tension supported by the clip.
written.sourceEvidence: The dialogue includes tensions about uniforms and rival groups.
